short: Event input and a two-step OT-CFM decoder are standard; the DVS-Lip evaluation is behind: WER on an isolated-word set with no split details or seeds, and baselines that do not match their sources.
position: The paper [@chen2026lipsflow] changes two components: event-stream input (M05, standard: DVS-Lip already supplies camera events) and a two-step OT-CFM text decoder (M06, standard: 0.2 WER points over its own diffusion variant, one run). Its evaluation (M12) is behind the field: DVS-Lip is a 100-word isolated-word set with one speaker per clip, scored by word accuracy on a speaker-disjoint split [@tan2022mstp]; the paper cites that protocol (Sec. 5.1) but calls the set multi-speaker and reports WER and VER with no split details, seeds or intervals. The baseline tables do not hold together: Table 2 sets AVA "Clean" equal to the Table 1 DVS-Lip results for six methods, MSTP is listed 2.6 WER points worse than its published accuracy implies (inference), and the SynthVSR row carries the timing of the authors' own 50-step diffusion decoder, so the headline speed claim compares the paper with its own ablation. The low-light claim rests on events converted from the same RGB frames and shows no event-sensor advantage.
